sentences.en: There's an episode of the TV show Futurama where the protagonists discover that cats are actually aliens, conquering aliens that have come from another planet,
sentences.zh: 有一集电视节目《飞出个未来》，主角们发现猫其实是外星人，是从另一个星球来的征服外星人，

sentences.en: and conquered humanity into caring for them.
sentences.zh: 并且把人类征服了，让1人类照顾它们。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast episode 31, recorded on June 5th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 31 期，录制于 2021 年 6 月 5 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we continue part three of our four-part conversation with Chandler Carruth and Patricia Ass.
sentences.zh: 我叫康纳，今天我的联合主持人是布莱斯，我们继续与钱德勒·卡鲁斯和帕特里夏·阿斯进行四部分对话的第三部分。

sentences.en: On today's episode, we talk about strategic decision-making, how to disagree, and so much more.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们讨论战略决策、如何产生分歧以及更多内容。

sentences.en: If you haven't listened to parts one and two, they will be linked in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没听过第一部分和第二部分，它们会链接在节目笔记中。

sentences.en: I highly recommend you listen to those ones first, as this is a continuation of that conversation.
sentences.zh: 我强烈建议你先听那些，因为这是那场对话的延续。

sentences.en: So, I'm just curious.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只是好奇。

sentences.en: Should we try and get back to the actual questions, or do you want to just keep going?
sentences.zh: 我们是应该尝试回到实际问题上，还是你想继续说下去？

sentences.en: So, Mr. Carruth, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，卡鲁斯先生，好吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, one of the points here is not overcoming resistance to a directional change.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里的要点之一不是克服对方向转变的阻力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: Can you put that in an example, explain how you would go about that?
sentences.zh: 你能举个例子，解释一下你将如何着手处理吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I think this is – so, first off, let's make sure we understand what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这是——首先，让我们确保我们明白我们在谈论什么。

sentences.en: We're talking about times when there's, you know, there's a strategic decision or a directional decision that needs to happen,
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论有时候，你知道，有一个战略决策或方向决策需要做出，

sentences.en: and you have – you are suggesting and you are proposing a particular direction, and that is not the direction taken, right?
sentences.zh: 而你——你正在建议并提出一个特定的方向，但那并不是最终采取的方向，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you still need to – like, you need to – like, we're in the kind of disagree and commit phase.
sentences.zh: 而你仍然需要——就像，你需要——就像，我们处于“有异议但执行”的阶段。

sentences.en: But it's not about, like, doing a single thing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说，比如，只做一件事。

sentences.en: It's about, like, a very large-scale directional shift.
sentences.zh: 这是关于，比如，非常大规模的方向转变。

sentences.en: And I've seen this a couple of times, and I've had this happen to me a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 我见过好几次这种情况，我自己也经历过好几次。

sentences.en: So, the particular – like, one of the particular sharp examples here is there's a technology that I do not personally kind of like.
sentences.zh: 所以，具体——比如，这里的一个具体而尖锐的例子是，有一种技术我个人其实不太喜欢。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem elegant to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来它不够优雅。

sentences.en: And it's called ThinLTO.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 ThinLTO。

sentences.en: This is a variation of link-time optimization developed by Teresa Jackson and David Lee and a bunch of other people at Google.
sentences.zh: 这是由特雷萨·杰克逊、大卫·李和谷歌的一群其他人开发的一种链接时间优化变体。

sentences.en: And personally, I don't like the way it works.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我不喜欢它的工作方式。

sentences.en: It seems like a messy workaround.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一个杂乱的权宜之计。

sentences.en: And so, I advocated really hard that we should actually invest in understanding why.
sentences.zh: 因此，我非常努力地主张我们应该真正投资去了解为什么。

sentences.en: But the goal of it is to make link-time optimization scalable enough to use broadly on very, very large C++ applications, huge C++ applications.
sentences.zh: 但它的目标是使链接时间优化具有足够的扩展性，以便在非常非常大的 C++ 应用程序、巨大的 C++ 应用程序上广泛使用。

sentences.en: And LTO normally, as it normally is, just doesn't scale very well.
sentences.zh: 而且通常情况下的 LTO，正如它通常的那样，扩展性根本不是很好。

sentences.en: And so, you can't use it for these applications.
sentences.zh: 因此，你不能将它用于这些应用程序。

sentences.en: And ThinLTO scales very well.
sentences.zh: 而 ThinLTO 的扩展性非常好。

sentences.en: I had argued that we should actually try and tackle the underlying scaling issues of LTO rather than taking the ThinLTO approach.
sentences.zh: 我曾争辩说，我们应该真正尝试解决 LTO 底层的扩展问题，而不是采用 ThinLTO 的方法。

sentences.en: I thought it was much more clean.
sentences.zh: 我认为这要干净得多。

sentences.en: I think there's a lot of really exciting untapped potential in that space.
sentences.zh: 我认为该领域有许多真正令人兴奋、尚未开发的潜力。

sentences.en: Basically, every link-time optimizing compiler that we had access to, which was basically one and a half LLVMs and some early-stage work in GCC at the time,
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们能接触到的每一个链接时间优化编译器，当时基本上是一个半 LLVM 和 GCC 中的一些早期阶段工作，

sentences.en: was single-threaded, right, and built around link lists.
sentences.zh: 都是单线程的，对吧，并且围绕链表构建。

sentences.en: And so, like, has the worst cache locality you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像，拥有你能想象到的最差的缓存局部性。

sentences.en: And so, it doesn't scale well, which is kind of unsurprising.
sentences.zh: 因此，它扩展性不好，这可以说是意料之中的。

sentences.en: And I was like, we need to fix those problems before we try and kind of change the fundamental model to make it scale.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，在试图改变基本模型以使其具有可扩展性之前，我们需要解决这些问题。

sentences.en: But Teresa and David had a great idea for how to change the fundamental model.
sentences.zh: 但特雷萨和大卫对如何改变基本模型有一个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: And it didn't require changing all of the internals of the compiler.
sentences.zh: 并且它不需要改变编译器的所有内部结构。

sentences.en: It didn't require, you know, making things, you know, multi-threaded and efficient and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 它不需要，你知道，让事情，你知道，变成多线程、高效以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And it still scales.
sentences.zh: 而且它仍然具有可扩展性。

sentences.en: And the decision was to basically go with their approach.
sentences.zh: 决定的结果基本上是采用他们的方法。

sentences.en: It was – and at the time, I really disagreed with this.
sentences.zh: 那是——在当时，我真的非常不同意这一点。

sentences.en: I thought this was just the wrong thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是做错了。

sentences.en: And it was kind of hard because, right, like, I had to help them out.
sentences.zh: 而且这有点难，对吧，因为我必须帮助他们。

sentences.en: I was bringing up LLVM at Google, having brought up Clang as the front end.
sentences.zh: 我在谷歌推出了 LLVM，并且已经推出了 Clang 作为前端。

sentences.en: I was bringing up kind of the LLVM back end for actual compilation.
sentences.zh: 我正在为实际编译推出某种 LLVM 后端。

sentences.en: And they were working on ThinLto and needed my support in LLVM.
sentences.zh: 而他们正在开发 ThinLTO 并且在 LLVM 中需要我的支持。

sentences.en: And that was hard for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我很艰难。

sentences.en: I struggled at firSt.
sentences.zh: 起初我很挣扎。

sentences.en: And largely, I think finally we got to a much better place where I found ways that I could kind of contribute to enabling them rather than kind of getting in their way.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上，我想我们最终来到了一个好得多的地方，我找到了能够为他们赋能而不是阻碍他们的方法。

sentences.en: But it was difficult.
sentences.zh: 但那确实很困难。

sentences.en: And the funny thing is that, like, in retrospect, right, like, if today me got past me and Teresa and David Lee's kind of different proposals, I would absolutely pick ThinLto.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，回想起来，对吧，如果今天的我和特雷萨以及大卫·李的不同提案交锋，我绝对会选择 ThinLTO。

sentences.en: So as much as it's less elegant, it's also dramatically less risky.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管它不那么优雅，但它的风险也大大降低了。

sentences.en: And at the time, I felt like I really didn't see this risk that was associated with the direction I was pushing for.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，我觉得自己真的没有看到与我所推动的方向相关的这种风险。

sentences.en: But in retrospect, it actually makes a lot more sense why we ended up going that direction.
sentences.zh: 但回过头来看，我们最终走向那个方向其实更有道理。

sentences.en: I think it was the right call, even though personally it felt really like, oh, this is a good technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是正确的决定，尽管个人感觉真的像是，哦，这是一项好技术。

sentences.en: And it also worked.
sentences.zh: 而且它也确实管用。

sentences.en: And for me, the biggest part of this kind of disagreeing committing at the strategic level was, you know, I had a loud voice in the LVM community.
sentences.zh: 对我和在战略层面上这种“有异议但执行”的最大部分来说，你知道，我在 LLVM 社区中很有发言权。

sentences.en: And it was important to actually acknowledge, like, this is working.
sentences.zh: 承认这一点非常重要，比如，这确实行之有效。

sentences.en: I had to do that very loudly.
sentences.zh: 我不得不非常大声地表达这一点。

sentences.en: And so, you know, making sure, like, Teresa could get up on a panel to talk about LTO.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，要确保，比如，特雷萨能够上台谈论 LTO。

sentences.en: So I got invited to a panel.
sentences.zh: 所以我被邀请参加一个小组讨论。

sentences.en: I was like, you should probably also bring Teresa up because, like, you know, I advocated for a different strategy of LTO.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，你大概也应该把特雷萨带上，因为，你知道的，我曾倡导过一种不同的 LTO 策略。

sentences.en: And hers is the one that actually got built.
sentences.zh: 而她的策略才是真正被构建出来的那个。

sentences.en: So maybe we should not.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们不应该……

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like, and doing that is, you know, it can feel bad.
sentences.zh: 比如，这样做，你知道，会让人感觉不好。

sentences.en: But that's the important part of kind of disagreeing committing at a strategic level is that you actually have to own the strategy at the end of it.
sentences.zh: 但在战略层面上，“有异议但执行”的重要部分在于，你最终必须对这一战略负责。

sentences.en: And because it's a strategic thing, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个战略问题，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not just like you're going to let the patch go in.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是说你要放行这个补丁。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You have to contribute to the new strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 你必须为新战略做出贡献，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to help debug things.
sentences.zh: 你必须帮助调试。

sentences.en: You have to help with the planning.
sentences.zh: 你必须协助规划。

sentences.en: You have to, like, figure out how the piece of, you know, LVM that I'm working on can actually call it, like, work with the thin LTO strategy, how to integrate this stuff.
sentences.zh: 你必须，比如，弄清楚我正在开发的 LLVM 的那部分代码如何才能真正调用它、如何与 ThinLTO 策略协同工作、如何集成这些东西。

sentences.en: And kind of you have to pull yourself on board with that, even if it feels like the wrong strategy.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须让自己全身心投入其中，即使感觉策略是错的。

sentences.en: But your negativity towards the concept probably spread to people around you as well.
sentences.zh: 但你对这个概念的消极情绪可能也蔓延到了你周围的人身上。

sentences.en: Because we are, you know, we are tribal in how we work.
sentences.zh: 因为我们，你知道，我们在工作时是有宗派主义的。

sentences.en: We are in our groups.
sentences.zh: 我们处在各自的圈子里。

sentences.en: Oh, of course.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: So did that cause any friction when you were trying to?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否在你试图……时引起了任何摩擦？

sentences.en: I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定。

sentences.en: I'm sure it did.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定确实如此。

sentences.en: And, like, I can remember specific places where it did.
sentences.zh: 而且，比如，我能记起它确实发生过的那种具体地方。

sentences.en: Because there were people who really thought I was right and I should have been able to make this decision.
sentences.zh: 因为有些人真的认为我是对的，而且我本应该能够做出这个决定。

sentences.en: And one of the interesting things, and again, this is a great observation, right?
sentences.zh: 其中有趣的一点是，再次说明，这是一个很好的观察，对吧？

sentences.en: Because when you want to actually overcome this kind of having a direction that you don't agree with being decided on.
sentences.zh: 因为当你真正想要克服这种“决定了一个你并不同意的方向”的情况时。

sentences.en: You actually have to undo that negativity.
sentences.zh: 你实际上必须消除那种消极情绪。

sentences.en: You can't prevent it.
sentences.zh: 你无法阻止它发生。

sentences.en: Like, there's no hope, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，没有希望，对吧？

sentences.en: People are going to, as you said, this is a natural thing.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，人们会有这种情绪，这是很自然的事情。

sentences.en: But you have to figure out how do you undo that.
sentences.zh: 但你必须弄清楚如何去消除它。

sentences.en: And one of the ways that you undo that, for example, is by going and doing the work, right?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，消除这种情绪的方法之一就是去付诸行动，把工作做好，对吧？

sentences.en: Do the groundwork, the dirty, grungy work, to actually help out the direction you didn't want.
sentences.zh: 去做基础工作，那些繁琐、肮脏的工作，去真正协助那个你并不想要的方向。

sentences.en: And let people see that, right?
sentences.zh: 并让人们看到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Because that helps people then understand that, like, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 因为这有助于人们随后理解，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: If Chandler's okay with it, then I guess it's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果钱德勒觉得没问题，那我想这就没问题。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like, and you have to be an active participant in kind of undoing that tribal stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如，你必须成为消除这种宗派主义情绪的积极参与者。

sentences.en: Yeah, because there will be people who will feel an intense loyalty to you.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为会有一些人对你怀有强烈的忠诚感。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，因此，是的。

sentences.en: I also want to be clear.
sentences.zh: 我也想澄清一点。

sentences.en: I don't think I handled this particular case perfectly.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我把这个特定案例处理得完美无缺。

sentences.en: Part of why I'm bringing this one up is that this one was probably one of the rougher cases.
sentences.zh: 我提起这个案例的部分原因在于，这可能是最棘手的案例之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think there's still kind of ruffled feathers.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为仍然存在一些不愉快的情绪。

sentences.en: And it still is difficult for people who are on different sides of this to kind of work effectively.
sentences.zh: 而且对于站在不同立场上的人来说，高效合作仍然很困难。

sentences.en: And we all lose as a consequence, right?
sentences.zh: 结果我们所有人都输了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, that's not a good outcome.
sentences.zh: 比如，那不是一个好的结果。

sentences.en: Is there a way that you could have handled it differently that could have maybe given a better result?
sentences.zh: 有没有一种方法，你可以用不同的方式处理它，从而可能带来更好的结果？

sentences.en: I should have been much more vocal earlier.
sentences.zh: 我本应该更早地大声说出来。

sentences.en: So there was a lot of lag time between kind of the decision getting made and when I was able to kind of, you know, do some of this legwork to support it.
sentences.zh: 因此，从做出决定到我能够去，你知道，做一些基础工作来支持它之间，存在着大量的滞后时间。

sentences.en: And I think that really amplified a lot of the probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实放大了许多问题。

sentences.en: And what would have been better would have been to have kind of very immediate, like, decision made and immediately show signs of, like, helping implement the new decision.
sentences.zh: 更好的做法是进行非常直接的干预，比如，做出决定并立即表现出迹象，比如帮助落实新的决策。

sentences.en: But for me, like, when I read these things, it seems like an upward thing towards management that I have to get on board with this thing because the decision has been made.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，当我读到这些内容时，它似乎是对管理层的一种迎合，因为决策已经做出，我必须接受这件事。

sentences.en: And, you know, so that the management or whoever's above me will see that I'm a team player.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，好让管理层或任何在我之上的人看到我是一个团队合作者。

sentences.en: And that doesn't resound much with me.
sentences.zh: 这并没有引起我的多少共鸣。

sentences.en: But what you're saying is more that I need to show these people who are loyal to me and who respect me that, you know, I'm okay with this and we should be okay with this together.
sentences.zh: 但你所说的更多是，我需要向那些忠于我、尊重我的人展示，你知道，我对此没意见，我们应该一起对此没意见。

sentences.en: And we should, you know, yeah, that makes much more sense to me.
sentences.zh: 而且我们应该，你知道，是的，这对我来说更有意义。

sentences.en: And it's wild the effects this has, like, this, you know, that delay, which I still really regret to this day, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这产生的效果太疯狂了，比如，那个延迟，我至今仍然深感后悔，对吧？

sentences.en: It hurt team morale, right?
sentences.zh: 它伤害了团队士气，对吧？

sentences.en: It caused, you know, parts of the team to drift apart, right?
sentences.zh: 它导致，你知道，团队的一部分人分崩离析，对吧？

sentences.en: How many missed opportunities were there because we let this friction, and I say we, like, because I was part of this, right?
sentences.zh: 错失了多少机会，只因为我们任由这种摩擦滋生，我用“我们”是因为我也是其中的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: We let this friction develop.
sentences.zh: 我们任由这种摩擦发展。

sentences.en: And it's got to be a lot.
sentences.zh: 这一定有很多。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, it's a regret.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一种遗憾。

sentences.en: There's a part of my soul is sad that I'm bringing this up, but it is a good leadership principle.
sentences.zh: 我的心灵深处有一部分在为提起这件事感到难过，但它确实是一个很好的领导力原则。

sentences.en: So there's, at Amazon, there's these 14 LPs, which stands for leadership principles.
sentences.zh: 所以，在亚马逊，有 14 条 LP，代表领导力原则（Leadership Principles）。

sentences.en: And Amazon is famous for, you know, really promoting these across culture and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊以在文化等各方面大力推广这些原则而闻名。

sentences.en: And one of them is disagree and commit.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是“有异议但执行”（disagree and commit）。

sentences.en: And it's actually a pretty good one.
sentences.zh: 而且它实际上是一个相当不错的原则。

sentences.en: Some of them I don't agree with all 14 of them, but this one, it's basically like there's going to be times where there's different directions that you can go,
sentences.zh: 虽然并不是 14 条我都完全赞同，但这一条，基本上就像是会有这样的时刻：你可以走向不同的方向，

sentences.en: either technically or strategically.
sentences.zh: 无论是在技术上还是在战略上。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're really big on data-driven design and stuff like that at Amazon.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们在亚马逊非常热衷于数据驱动的设计之类的事情。

sentences.en: But at a certain point, a decision has to be made.
sentences.zh: 但在某个特定时间点，必须做出决定。

sentences.en: And basically the LP talks about how once that decision is made, you can say, you know, I don't agree with this decision.
sentences.zh: 基本上该 LP 谈到，一旦做出决定，你可以说，你知道，我不同意这个决定。

sentences.en: I think it's, you know, I prefer this one, but we're going with this one.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是，你知道，我更喜欢这个，但我们要选那个。

sentences.en: And once that decision is made, like, it's supposed to be like everyone's on board with it, commits to it, and they're going to make that successful and work.
sentences.zh: 而一旦做出决定，就像，它应该意味着每个人都支持它、致力于它，并努力使其取得成功和运作。

sentences.en: And there's an opportunity to sort of state that, like, I don't agree with this final decision.
sentences.zh: 并且有机会公开表态，比如，我不同意这个最后的决定。

sentences.en: But once that decision is made, it's time to, you know, go forward.
sentences.zh: 但一旦做出决定，就是时候，你知道，向前看了。

sentences.en: And, yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的。

sentences.en: I don't know how easy that is to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这做起来有多容易。

sentences.en: And it's definitely not easy, but, like, having that as an LP at a company, like, as a sort of a tenant, like,
sentences.zh: 它绝对不容易，但是，在公司里把这作为一个 LP，作为一个某种信条，就像是，

sentences.en: I definitely have worked at companies where those disagreements happen, and then they just sort of, like, they just linger.
sentences.zh: 我确实在一些公司工作过，在那些地方会出现这种分歧，然后它们就会一直拖延下去。

sentences.en: And it's not even clear, like, you know, how do we come to the decision?
sentences.zh: 甚至连我们究竟是怎么做出决定的都搞不清楚。

sentences.en: And so they just sort of, it goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 所以它们就会没完没了地持续下去。

sentences.en: And it's, I think it's a great sort of tenant to have that, like, you know, there's inevitably at any company there's going to be disagreements.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，有一个很好的核心准则，那就是在任何公司都不可避免地会出现分歧。

sentences.en: But at a certain point, you just got to pull the trigger, and everyone's got to contribute to that direction at that point.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，你必须当机立断，从那一刻起，每个人都要朝着那个方向出力。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe a year down the road, you'll figure out it wasn't the right decision, and you can reassess at that point.
sentences.zh: 而且，也许一年之后你会发现这不是个正确的决定，到那时你可以重新评估。

sentences.en: But, you know, for that year when you're getting to that point, it doesn't help to sort of, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在为达到那个目标而努力的那一年里，如果团队中只有50%的人

sentences.en: have only 50% of the team that believes that that was the right decision to be really, you know, all cylinders ahead on it or have 50% not all cylinders ahead.
sentences.zh: 相信那是正确的决定并全力以赴，或者只有50%的人全力以赴，这对事情并没有帮助。

sentences.en: You know, that's not helpful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这毫无帮助。

sentences.en: You're going to realize the decision was the wrong one, if it was the wrong one, faster, if everyone is just helping out.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都齐心协力，你会更快地发现这个决定是否错误（如果它确实是错的话）。

sentences.en: And I want to be very clear about something.
sentences.zh: 我想明确说明一点。

sentences.en: Having a tenant is important.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个核心准则很重要。

sentences.en: But taking it back to Patricia, right, the questions, like, for interviewing someone in a leadership role,
sentences.zh: 但回到帕特里夏的话题，对吧？当我们在面试担任领导角色的人时，

sentences.en: the particular key thing here is that people in this role need to really show that they are operating by the tenant.
sentences.zh: 这里特别关键的一点是，处于这个角色的人需要真正表现出他们是在遵循准则行事。

sentences.en: And that's even more important than the tenant itself.
sentences.zh: 而这甚至比准则本身更重要。

sentences.en: We have the tenant at Google, and it still happens because whenever there's a leader that isn't showing they're going to live by this tenant, it starts to cause, like,
sentences.zh: 我们在谷歌也有这个准则，但这种情况仍然会发生，因为每当有领导者表现出他们不会恪守这一准则时，就会开始引发……

sentences.en: it starts that entrenchment.
sentences.zh: 就会开始形成那种根深蒂固的僵局。

sentences.en: But I think it's a lot about the human condition.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这在很大程度上与人性有关。

sentences.en: We are often very proud people, and we also have lots of loyalty.
sentences.zh: 我们往往是非常自负的人，而且我们也有很强的忠诚度。

sentences.en: And having these things will make it difficult to say, okay, I loSt.
sentences.zh: 拥有这些特质会让人很难说出：“好吧，我输了。”

sentences.en: And also, I'm not only okay with losing, but I'm enthusiastically on board with you.
sentences.zh: 而且，不仅承认失败没关系，我还要满腔热情地支持你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: It's a great way of putting it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你这话讲得太好了，没错。

sentences.en: So some techniques that I've been trying to practice to help me overcome that human reluctance is to change the kind of frame of mind of what my goal is.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在尝试练习的一些技巧，来帮助自己克服这种人性的抗拒感，就是改变我目标的思维框架。

sentences.en: I'm not usually a huge fan of corporate trainings, right?
sentences.zh: 我通常不是企业培训的超级粉丝，对吧？

sentences.en: Sometimes they're real questionable.
sentences.zh: 有时它们真的很扯。

sentences.en: But there's one corporate training that I really love.
sentences.zh: 但我有一场非常喜欢的企业培训。

sentences.en: Even though most of it's garbage, it has this one catchphrase that I keep coming back to, which is, you know, what do you really, really want?
sentences.zh: 尽管大部分内容都是垃圾，但它有一个我总是铭记在心的口头禅，那就是：“你究竟、究竟想要什么？”

sentences.en: And then they clarify, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会澄清：不，不，不。

sentences.en: What is the one thing that you really want?
sentences.zh: 你真正想要的那唯一的东西是什么？

sentences.en: Like, you must choose one thing and focus on that.
sentences.zh: 就像，你必须选择一件事并专注于它。

sentences.en: And when you apply that here, the interesting thing you get to is what you really want is a decision.
sentences.zh: 当你把这个应用到这里时，你会发现一个有趣的事情：你真正想要的是一个决定。

sentences.en: Not your decision, but a decision.
sentences.zh: 不是你想要的决定，而是一个决定。

sentences.en: And so by focusing on the fact that you've made a decision, you're making progress,
sentences.zh: 因此，通过专注于“你已经做出了一个决定”这一事实，你就在取得进展，

sentences.en: you basically channel your enthusiasm for progress as proxy for the enthusiasm of the decision you don't particularly like, right?
sentences.zh: 你基本上是将你对“取得进展”的热情，转化为对那个你并不是特别喜欢的决定的热情的替代品，对吧？

sentences.en: And this kind of lets you get yourself enthusiastic and then apply it to something that you're not super enthusiastic about.
sentences.zh: 这种方法能让你自己充满热情，然后把它应用到那些你并不是那么热衷的事情上去。

sentences.en: Okay, so get a proxy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以找一个替代动力。

sentences.en: You realize, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你会意识到，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's all about picking, well, what do you really want?
sentences.zh: 这一切都在于选择：好吧，你到底想要什么？

sentences.en: Do you want your decision or do you want to have a decision?
sentences.zh: 你是想要你自己的决定，还是想要一个决定？

sentences.en: Because you can't always have both.
sentences.zh: 因为你不可能总是鱼和熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: So you have to pick which one you care about moSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须选择你最在乎的是哪个。

sentences.en: Once you do that, it's much easier to be enthusiastic about not having your decision because that's not what you're enthusiastic about.
sentences.zh: 一旦你做到了这一点，要对“没有按你的意愿做决定”保持热情就会容易得多，因为这不是你所热衷的焦点。

sentences.en: You're enthusiastic about making it through the decision, getting the decision, making people start moving in some direction, right?
sentences.zh: 你热衷的是把决定敲定下来，做出决让大家开始朝着某个方向前进，对吧？

sentences.en: And this, for me, was really helpful in part because I noticed something, and a manager of mine years and years ago told me this, and I didn't get it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这真的很有帮助，部分原因是我注意到了一件事——很多很多年前我的一个经理对我说过这话，当时我没听懂。

sentences.en: It didn't make sense at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时觉得这没道理。

sentences.en: But he pointed out that it is much cheaper in so many cases to let people make the decision they want to make than to convince them to make the decision you think is right.
sentences.zh: 但他指出，在很多情况下，让别人去做出他们想做的决定，要比说服他们去做你认为正确的决定成本低得多。

sentences.en: And then, to your point, Connor, eventually, if it is wrong, they'll figure it out.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，康纳，最终如果错了，他们自己会发现的。

sentences.en: It can be so much cheaper to let people make a bad decision and then learn what the right decision is than to try and prevent them from making a mistake or trying to avoid the wrong decision.
sentences.zh: 让人们做一个糟糕的决定，然后从中吸取教训，了解什么是正确的决定，往往比试图阻止他们犯错或试图避免做出错误决定要划算得多。

sentences.en: Just make the bad decision.
sentences.zh: 那就直接做出那个糟糕的决定吧。

sentences.en: It'll be totally fine.
sentences.zh: 完全没问题的。

sentences.en: We'll figure it out later.
sentences.zh: 我们以后再想办法解决。

sentences.en: And that can be so much lower cost, especially at larger scales.
sentences.zh: 而且这能大大降低成本，尤其是在规模更大的情况下。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I have a baby example from when I was like a super junior.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有一个非常初级的小例子，发生在我还是个超级菜鸟的时候。

sentences.en: I was at Opera, and we were working on the desktop browser, and we had this guy who was basically, I don't know, I guess in retrospect,
sentences.zh: 当时我在欧朋（Opera），我们正在开发桌面浏览器，我们团队里有这么一个人，基本上，我不知道，现在回想起来，

sentences.en: I would say he was like sort of like a creative genius, but he was also a coder.
sentences.zh: 我会说他有点像那种创意天才，但他同时也是个程序员。

sentences.en: And so he had created all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 所以他创造了各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And so basically a lot of what was Opera was basically his brainchild.
sentences.zh: 因此，基本上Opera的很大一部分可以说是他的心血结晶。

sentences.en: And so, and then he comes and he was like, he has this brilliant idea in his, like his opinion, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，他提出了一个点子，在他看来这是一个绝妙的点子。

sentences.en: And all of these people that, you know, worked with him for a long time, they, you know, he was like superhero.
sentences.zh: 所有那些跟他共事了很长时间的人，你知道的，他就像是个超级英雄。

sentences.en: They were like, this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他们都觉得：“这太绝了。”

sentences.en: And I thought it was dumb.
sentences.zh: 而我觉得这很蠢。

sentences.en: I was like, no, nobody's, this is silly.
sentences.zh: 我想：才不是呢，没人会……这太傻了。

sentences.en: Like, are we going to do this?
sentences.zh: 我们真的要这么做吗？

sentences.en: This is a really silly thing.
sentences.zh: 这真的是个很傻的想法。

sentences.en: And I was so wrong.
sentences.zh: 结果我大错特错。

sentences.en: I was like the wrongest in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 我简直是全世界错得最离谱的人。

sentences.en: Because what he, I don't know if anyone remembers, but way back when, in the early 2000s, when you opened a tab, it was white.
sentences.zh: 因为他提出的那个点子——不知道是否有人还记得，在遥远的2000年代初期，当你打开一个标签页时，它是一片空白。

sentences.en: There was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 里面什么也没有。

sentences.en: It was just a white rectangle in your face.
sentences.zh: 迎面而来的只有一个白色的矩形。

sentences.en: And his idea was, let's put like big icons and things there for your favorite websites.
sentences.zh: 而他的想法是：让我们在那里放一些大图标之类的东西，用来放置你最喜欢的网站。

sentences.en: And he called it a speed dial.
sentences.zh: 他把这叫做“快速拨号”（speed dial）。

sentences.en: And it would have like the nine, like a speed dial.
sentences.zh: 它会有九个格子，就像电话的快速拨号一样。

sentences.en: And he would even connect it to, see if you tap the right, like number, it would open that.
sentences.zh: 他甚至把它连接到……如果你按下对应的数字键，它就会打开那个网站。

sentences.en: But you could also click on them.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以直接点击它们。

sentences.en: And so you had like a three by three matrix where you could put in all of your favorite websites with like a picture and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有一个三乘三的矩阵，可以在里面放入你所有喜欢的网站，配有图片什么的。

sentences.en: And so when he opened a new tab, you would see the speed dial and you could just click on where you want it to go.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你打开一个新标签页时，你会看到快速拨号，只需点击你想去的地方即可。

sentences.en: I was like, this is silly.
sentences.zh: 当时我觉得：这太蠢了。

sentences.en: This is stupid.
sentences.zh: 这太笨了。

sentences.en: It's like, I was, I was so wrong.
sentences.zh: 真的，我当时错得太离谱了。

sentences.en: I was, I was absolutely, completely, terribly wrong about this entire thing.
sentences.zh: 我对整件事情的看法完全、彻底、错得一塌糊涂。

sentences.en: And, and, and for me personally, this was huge for me because, and it's colored like my entire thinking for the rest of my career, because I learned that I can be fundamentally,
sentences.zh: 而且，对我个人而言，这意义重大，因为这件事影响了我整个职业生涯余下时间的思维方式，因为我了解到，我对某事的看法可能会错得彻底，

sentences.en: completely wrong about something and have no idea.
sentences.zh: 完全离谱，而我自己却浑然不知。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, and because I think we have this tendency to believe in ourselves.
sentences.zh: 就像，因为我们往往倾向于坚信自己。

sentences.en: Like I, you know, I think this is dumb and I will, all data I will find will reaffirm my, my position.
sentences.zh: 就像我，你知道，我觉得这很蠢，而且我会寻找所有数据来印证我的立场。

sentences.en: And I would kind of hold on to it no matter what happens.
sentences.zh: 不管发生什么，我都会坚持己见。

sentences.en: But actually sitting down and like accepting the fact that this was brilliant and it has been copied by all browsers ever since.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，静下心来接受这个事实：这个点子简直天才，并且自那以后被所有的浏览器竞相模仿。

sentences.en: You know, it's, you know, it's like 15 years later, this is what you do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，15年过去了，这成了标准做法。

sentences.en: But, but, but so, so it was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以，它确实是个天才的想法。

sentences.en: But having that gave me the, the, the, I don't know, I, I, I won't call it humility because it's not humility.
sentences.zh: 但拥有了这种经历，给了我……我不知道，我不会称之为谦逊，因为这并非谦逊。

sentences.en: It's, it's a healthy skepticism to, to my own, like, opinion.
sentences.zh: 这是对自我观点的一种健康的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: And a willingness just to like be wrong and, and like, and see that like good things can happen even when you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 并且愿意承认自己犯错，看到即使在你犯错的时候，也可能会发生美好的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just like, okay, so this is what I think I might be wrong.
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，这就是我的想法，我可能搞错了。

sentences.en: Like there might be like a fundamental flaw here where I'm just totally wrong.
sentences.zh: 这里可能存在一个根本性的缺陷，导致我完全想错了。

sentences.en: And if I am, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那也没关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's like a superpower.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种超能力。

sentences.en: If you, if you can actually go walk into a room and be convinced by someone else and like really,
sentences.zh: 如果你真的能够走进一个房间，被别人说服，并且真正地、

sentences.en: truly convinced that I think that what you said was right and what I said was wrong, that, that can build like mountains.
sentences.zh: 发自内心地被说服——认为你说的是对的，而我说的是错的——那能够创造出排山倒海的力量。

sentences.en: Like it's, it's, it's, you, it's massive and it's such a small thing.
sentences.zh: 这真的是太巨大了，虽然它只是件小事。

sentences.en: I do this.
sentences.zh: 我也这样做过。

sentences.en: I, I, I, I freely admit I struggle with this.
sentences.zh: 我坦白承认，我在这方面也很挣扎。

sentences.en: That's why I cheat.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我要“作弊”。

sentences.en: I cheat by focusing on, on, on, uh, you know, progress over.
sentences.zh: 我通过专注于……你知道的，把进展置于……以此来作弊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I, I think that's a good one because I think that's something that, you know, you can do because it hurts to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个好方法，因为我觉得这是你能做到的事，毕竟承认错误很痛苦。

sentences.en: It sucks to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 犯错的感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: It really does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: This is coming up because literally just on the last episode, Bryce remarked the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 这个话题之所以浮现，是因为就在上一集里，布莱斯（Bryce）也表达了完全相同的观点。

sentences.en: That is a telltale sign of, um, really bright folks is the ability to like, once they've realized that they're wrong,
sentences.zh: 真正聪明的人的一个显著标志就是，一旦他们意识到自己错了，

sentences.en: just to like unabashedly like change 180 degrees and start 90 degrees and start walking that direction as if like they never at any point previously thought otherwise, like they'd,
sentences.zh: 就能毫不脸红地直接来个180度大转弯，开始朝另一个方向前行，表现得好像他们在此之前从没持过相反意见一样……

sentences.en: Oh, I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 哦，我错了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那没问题。

sentences.en: With credit.
sentences.zh: 欣然接受。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And yeah, something, something you were saying earlier, and this sort of goes to the, your example, Patricia is I, I'm not, I actually don't think this is an Amazon thing,
sentences.zh: 还有，你刚才说的某些内容，这有点符合你举的例子，帕特里夏，其实我不觉得这算亚马逊的专利，

sentences.en: but I learned it in Amazon.
sentences.zh: 但我确实是在亚马逊学到这一点的。

sentences.en: They have this policy of like one way and two way door to decisions.
sentences.zh: 他们对决策有一种“单向门”和“双向门”的政策。

sentences.en: And that like, if it's a two way door decision, meaning that you can enter and then leave, um, those are the ones where it's a lot easier to just like, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果这是一个双向门的决定，意味着你可以进去也可以出来，嗯，这种决定就容易得多，只需……你知道的，

sentences.en: disagree and commit.
sentences.zh: “有分歧但依然服从”（disagree and commit）。

sentences.en: And we'll find out.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: And that's the thing is like designing that sort of nine, three by three icon.
sentences.zh: 就像设计那种九宫格、三乘三的图标一样。

sentences.en: If it's a terrible idea at the end of the day, you just, you just trash it.
sentences.zh: 如果到头来这真是个糟糕的主意，你大不了把它扔掉就是了。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: There's a sunk cost there, but like there's, there's very, very little cost to like reversing that.
sentences.zh: 其中会有沉没成本，但推翻它的成本非常非常低。

sentences.en: And there's certain decisions where it's one way, if you're going to make this big change.
sentences.zh: 但有些决定是单向的，如果你要做出这种重大的改变。

sentences.en: And those are the ones that you really have to spend a ton of time up front, you know, figuring out, is this the direction?
sentences.zh: 这些才是你真正需要花大量时间在前期去弄清楚“这到底是不是正确方向”的决定。

sentences.en: Although Chandler, you're, you're saying maybe not even that one.
sentences.zh: 尽管钱德勒（Chandler），你的意思是可能连这种也不需要？

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Like, I think, I think that's, that's, that's actually a critical flaw.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这其实是一个致命的缺陷。

sentences.en: The goal shouldn't be to spend a ton of time up front, figuring out the right decision.
sentences.zh: 目标不应该是在前期花大量时间去找出正确的决定。

sentences.en: When you have a one way decision, the goal should be to engineer the door to open the other direction.
sentences.zh: 当你面临一个单向决定的决策时，你的目标应该是把这扇门设计成可以朝另一个方向打开。

sentences.en: Yeah, the goal should be the one, one way decisions are never good.
sentences.zh: 对，目标应该……单向决定从来都不是什么好东西。

sentences.en: Like what, what, what the, the classical example of this is standard C++, like the, one of the big problems,
sentences.zh: 就像经典的例子标准C++那样，其中一个重大问题在于，

sentences.en: the standard C++ has that pretty much all of our decisions are one way decisions.
sentences.zh: 标准C++几乎所有的决定都是单向决定。

sentences.en: And we would have a lot less stress if, if we could find ways to have that not be the case.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能找到方法避免这种情况，我们的压力就会小得多。

sentences.en: This is something that, that I see in API design all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是我在API设计中经常看到的情况。

sentences.en: A lot of people feel like, you know, an API is a one way decision because once you publish it, you have to support it forever.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得，API是一个单向决定，因为一旦你发布了它，你就得永远维护下去。

sentences.en: And, and so, so then a bunch of people invest incredible amounts of time trying to do good API design and to avoid mistakes.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多人投入了大量的时间来试图做好API设计并避免犯错。

sentences.en: And, and my perspective has really been warped here to, to a different thing where it's like, I mean, sure, invest some amount of time there,
sentences.zh: 而我的观点真的已经被扭转到了另一个方向，那就是：当然，你可以投入一定的时间，

sentences.en: but you almost want to time box that very sharply and instead invest all of the rest of the time in getting out of the mistakes that you will inevitably make.
sentences.zh: 但你几乎应该严格限制这些时间，并将剩下的所有时间都投入到如何摆脱你不可避免会犯的错误中去。

sentences.en: Um, because one of these things is, is, is, has a different scaling function on it than the other one, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这两者在规模扩展上的规律是完全不同的，对吧？

sentences.en: If you, if you invest a bunch of time making a good decision, that's one way, great.
sentences.zh: 如果你，如果你投入大量时间做出一个好决定，那是一种方式，很好。

sentences.en: But the next one, right?
sentences.zh: 但下一个呢？

sentences.en: Like it doesn't, none of that investment pays off for the next decision you have to make.
sentences.zh: 就像它不会，这种投入对你接下来要做的决定没有任何帮助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Whereas if you invest a bunch of time making the door two ways, all of that time you invest pays off every time you get the decision where that door applies.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你花大量时间把门做成双向的，你投入的所有时间都会在你遇到适用那扇门的决定时得到回报。

sentences.en: Um, and so it's, it's a tremendously better scaling function.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这是一个，这是一个规模化效果好得多的函数。

sentences.en: And so you time box the non-scaling investment, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你给非规模化投入设定了时间盒，对吧？

sentences.en: And put all of the rest of the energy into, into changing the, the, the problem space.
sentences.zh: 然后把剩下的所有精力都投入到，投入到改变，改变，改变问题空间中。

sentences.en: That's a great point.
sentences.zh: 这真是个好观点。

sentences.en: It's just, it's basically like from finance or business, it's fixed versus variable costs.
sentences.zh: 这就像，这基本上就像金融或商业里的固定成本与可变成本。

sentences.en: Like you, you do the two way door and it's variable.
sentences.zh: 就像你，你做双向门，它是可变的。

sentences.en: And then that just distributes over every single decision you make in the future.
sentences.zh: 然后这就会分摊到你在未来做出的每一个决定上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I've actually, that's a, it's a great meta point.
sentences.zh: 我其实，这是一个，这是一个很棒的元观点。

sentences.en: Like Amazon, you should update your book, update, update your stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像亚马逊，你们应该更新你们的书，更新，更新你们的东西。

sentences.en: But there's another kind of other subtle problem here, uh, which is the time spent before a decision is made is the most expensive time.
sentences.zh: 但这里还有另一种微妙的问题，呃，也就是在做出决定之前花费的时间是最昂贵的时间。

sentences.en: So one of the interesting things about spending your engineering time on the doors instead of on the decisions is that you make the decision more rapidly.
sentences.zh: 所以关于把工程时间花在门上而不是决定上的一个有趣之处在于，你能更快地做出决定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So you time box your investment in the decision, you make the decision rapidly and that, that has its own value, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你给决定上的投入设定了时间盒，你迅速做出决定，这，这本身就有价值，对吧？

sentences.en: And you're not paying for an unmade decision the entire time you're investing in doing the door.
sentences.zh: 而且在你花时间做这扇门的全过程中，你不用为尚未做出的决定付代价。

sentences.en: You're just making bad decisions.
sentences.zh: 你只是在做糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: So can I, can I take us down from metaphor to concrete?
sentences.zh: 那我可以，我能把我们从隐喻拉回到具体吗？

sentences.en: Like what is a door?
sentences.zh: 比如什么是门？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: Here.
sentences.zh: 给你。

sentences.en: So, so like classic example, let's take APIs.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以像经典例子，我们以API为例。

sentences.en: I think C++ APIs are a great example here, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为C++ API就是一个很好的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: We can, we can try to do good API design, but the, the thing we actually want to invest most of our time in is the ability to change the API when we get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们可以，我们可以尝试做好API设计，但我们真正想把大部分时间投入进去的，是当API搞砸时修改它的能力。

sentences.en: And so we build refactoring tools and then we build large scale refactoring tools and then we build systems for running large scale refactorings across a monolithic code base or across all of the shards of your sharded code base.
sentences.zh: 所以我们构建重构工具，然后我们构建大规模重构工具，然后我们构建系统，用于在单一代码库或你的分片代码库的所有分片上运行大规模重构。

sentences.en: And you, and then you tune that system so that you can run them more rapidly and at lower coSt.
sentences.zh: 然后你，接着你调整这个系统，以便你能更快、以更低的成本运行它们。

sentences.en: For example, at Google, one of our big costs is we're lucky we have a monolithic repository that we can handle, but we, we, we, we have to do code review.
sentences.zh: 例如，在谷歌，我们的巨大成本之一——幸运的是我们有一个能够处理的单一代码库——但我们，我们，我们必须进行代码审查。

sentences.en: And so we, we made, we're making 10,000 refactoring changes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，我们制作了，我们正在进行1万次重构变更。

sentences.en: How do you code review those?
sentences.zh: 你怎么对这些进行代码审查？

sentences.en: So we've actually built tools and infrastructure to smooth the code review cost and to bring that cost down, build tools to smooth the testing cost of rolling out these changes,
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上构建了工具和基础设施来平摊代码审查的成本并降低该成本，构建工具来平摊推出这些变更的测试成本，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And what we're doing is we're, because, because you almost never have true one-way doors.
sentences.zh: 而我们正在做的是，因为，因为你几乎永远不会有真正的单向门。

sentences.en: What you do is you have a differential cost function based on the direction, right?
sentences.zh: 你所做的是根据方向拥有一个差异化成本函数，对吧？

sentences.en: That it costs us so much money or time to go in and it costs us, you know, so like this massive multiplier if we ever want to go back out.
sentences.zh: 进去要花我们那么多钱或时间，而如果你想退出来，你知道，就会有这样一个巨大的乘数。

sentences.en: What you're actually trying to do is we're trying to drive that cost down over time.
sentences.zh: 你真正试图做的是，我们试图随着时间推移把这个成本降下来。

sentences.en: And we, we very specifically just attack the economic problem of replacing an API when we discover a mistake.
sentences.zh: 而且我们非常具体地只攻克在发现错误时替换API的经济问题。

sentences.en: And every time we make that cost lower, right?
sentences.zh: 每一次我们把那个成本降低，对吧？

sentences.en: This makes the kind of risk of each API decision lower because we're like, well, maybe we're wrong.
sentences.zh: 这就会降低每一个API决策的风险，因为我们会想，好吧，也许我们错了。

sentences.en: And so we can still apply some time boxed amount of, like there's still a differential here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍然可以应用一些设定了时间盒的量，就像这里依然存在差异。

sentences.en: It's not, it's not free, right?
sentences.zh: 它不是，它不是免费的，对吧？

sentences.en: But now we can have a much more rational time box around like, well, we've, we've, we've consulted the experts.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们可以围绕以下内容制定更理性的时间盒，比如，好吧，我们已经，我们已经，我们已经咨询过专家了。

sentences.en: We've thought about the consequences of this API design to the best of our ability.
sentences.zh: 我们已经尽我们最大能力考虑了这种API设计带来的后果。

sentences.en: It's going to, like, we think this is a good one.
sentences.zh: 它会，就像，我们认为这是一个好设计。

sentences.en: Let's try it out.
sentences.zh: 让我们试试看。

sentences.en: And if it doesn't work, we'll replace it, right?
sentences.zh: 如果不管用，我们就换掉它，对吧？

sentences.en: And even for a particular API, we, like you can, you can turtle this all the way down, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至对于特定的API，我们，就像你可以，你可以把这个层层嵌套下去，对吧？

sentences.en: So for a particular API, past a certain point, rather than trying to theorize about how the programmers will, will,
sentences.zh: 所以对于一个特定的API，过了某个时间点后，与其去理论化地推测程序员将如何，将会，

sentences.en: will react to this API and how readable or not readable it will be.
sentences.zh: 将会对这个API作出什么反应，以及它是否具有可读性。

sentences.en: If we're particularly uncertain, we'll actually invest in being able to roll back that particular API.
sentences.zh: 如果我们特别不确定，我们实际上会投入资金来实现回滚那个特定的API。

sentences.en: So we'll have, you know, an allow list early on for who gets to use it so that we can avoid it, you know, being everyone on day one, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们会，你知道的，在早期设立一个白名单，规定谁可以使用它，这样我们就可以避免它在第一天就变成所有人都在用，对吧？

sentences.en: And we can kind of have some beta testers and get some rounds of feedback.
sentences.zh: 我们可以有一些测试版用户并获得几轮反馈。

sentences.en: We may put special things into the API just to make it easier to change if we discover we're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会在API中加入一些特殊的东西，仅仅为了在我们发现自己错了时更容易修改。

sentences.en: And again, it's, and the whole thing here is just about decreasing the differential cost so that,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，整个事情的关键就在于降低差异化成本，以便，

sentences.en: so that we can make the decision and not worry about it and then learn and then make a new decision when, when we get new information.
sentences.zh: 以便我们能够做出决定而无需担心，然后去学习，并在获取新信息时做出新的决定。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢。

sentences.en: Stay tuned for part four, our final part of this conversation and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注第四部分，我们这次对话的最后一部分，祝你过愉快的一天。
